The problem is a design of a solid circular shaft using the angle-of-twist criterion in pure torsion.
The shaft is solid, circular, homogeneous, isotropic, and operates in the linear-elastic small-deformation regime.
The only load is a pure torque T = 1,000,000 N·mm applied uniformly along the shaft.
No transverse shear force, bending, buckling, fatigue, or stress-concentration effects are considered.
The shaft length is L = 1500 mm.
The shear modulus is G = 25,939.8 MPa (aluminum 6061-T6).
The allowable angle of twist is phi_allow = 0.75 degrees.
The governing relation is phi = (T * L) / (J * G), where J = (pi * d^4) / 32 for a solid circular cross-section.
The design task is to find the minimum shaft diameter d (in mm) such that phi <= phi_allow.
All quantities use a consistent unit system of Newtons, millimetres, and megapascals (N, mm, MPa).
No factor of safety or additional design criteria are to be applied; the minimum d is the value at which phi equals exactly 0.75 degrees.
Present the governing formula, solve algebraically for d, substitute all numerical values, and report the minimum diameter rounded up to a practical engineering value.
